sources.title: Shangri-La Songzanlin Monastery (Ganden Sumtseling Monastery) - China Highlights
sources.content:
Songzanlin Monastery - Complete Information

Overview
Songzanlin Monastery, also known as Ganden Sumtseling Monastery or Guihua Monastery, represents "the largest Tibetan Buddhist temple complex in Yunnan Province." It belongs to the Yellow Hat (Gelug) Sect and serves as the most important monastery for Tibetan worshippers across Yunnan, Sichuan, and southern central China.

Why Visit
The monastery earned the nickname "Little Potala Palace" because it was "Built after the Potala Palace in Lhasa." It functions as a Tibetan Art Museum, housing "gilded statues of Sakyamuni, palm-leaf scripts, thangka (religious tapestries), and golden lamps."

Currently, approximately 700 monks inhabit the monastery, down from 2,000 at its peak. Visitors can explore monk dormitories and interact with residents during advance-booked visits.

The Gedong Festival (month 11, day 29 of the Tibetan calendar) features spectacular religious mask dances called Cham dances performed by costumed monks.

History
Construction occurred "from 1679 to 1681 AD," with the Fifth Dalai Lama selecting the location through divination. The original structure was "destroyed during the cultural revolution in 1966" and rebuilt in 1982.

Architecture & Main Buildings
The monastery integrates "Tibetan and Han styles" in castle-like construction. Zhacang Hall serves as the central congregation space where monks study and chant, accommodating "more than 1,500 people" with 108 columns on the lower floor. Jikang Hall houses Zong Keba, the Gelug Sect founder.

Visiting Information
Location: Located "about 5 kilometers (3 miles) north of Shangri-La's city center" at Foping Mountain's base
Hours: 8am to 6pm
Altitude: 3,380 meters (11,090 feet)

Main Activities:
- Walking around Lamuyangcuo Lake (Virgin Soul Lake), approximately 50 minutes
- Exploring monastery halls and architecture
- Climbing Dongqusheng Hill for elevated views

Visitor Guidelines
- Remove sunglasses and hats when entering halls
- Walk clockwise (enter left, exit right)
- Avoid pointing at Buddha statues
- Photography is forbidden in all halls
- No loud speaking or smoking
- Drink water and move slowly due to altitude

sources.title: Songzanlin Monastery: Spiritual Haven of Tibetan Buddhism - ChinaXianTour
sources.content:
Songzanlin Monastery: Spiritual Haven of Tibetan Buddhism

Songzanlin Monastery, also known as Guihua Monastery, is the largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Yunnan, located just 5 kilometres away from the Shangri La / Zhongdian Old town. It is known as "Little Potala" according to its appearance.

It was built in 1679 and has been reconstructed several times as it is considered to be one of the most significant monasteries among Yunnan. Today, Songzanlin is the home for more or less 700 monks and Lamas for their monastic lives.

The monastery is composed of two lamaseries, Zhacang and Jikang. The gilded copper roof endows the monastery with strong Tibetan features and the 108 columns downstairs also feature it with characteristics of Han nationality.

Entry fee to the monastery: 75RMB per person + 15RMB per person for the shuttle. When arriving at Shangri-La Airport, hire a taxi to get to the Songzanlin Monastery within 20 minutes at a cost of CNY 25.

Spring and summer are the best seasons for people to visit it.

sources.title: Songzanlin Monastery - Tibetan Temple in Shangri La Yunnan
sources.content:
Songzanlin Monastery - Tibetan Temple in Shangri La Yunnan

Songzanlin Monastery is the largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Yunnan Province. Located about 5 km north of Shangri-La city center, it is often called the "Little Potala Palace" due to its architectural resemblance to the Potala Palace in Lhasa.

The monastery was founded in 1679 by the Fifth Dalai Lama and belongs to the Gelug (Yellow Hat) school of Tibetan Buddhism. It was largely destroyed during the Cultural Revolution but has been rebuilt since 1982.

The complex houses important religious artifacts including gilded Buddha statues, palm-leaf scriptures, thangka paintings, and golden lamps. About 700 monks currently reside in the monastery.

The monastery sits at an altitude of about 3,380 meters. Visitors should be prepared for the altitude and dress warmly, as temperatures can be cool even in summer.

sources.title: Songzanlin Monastery, Lamastery in Shangri La - Top China Travel
sources.content:
Songzanlin Monastery, Shangri-La

Songzanlin Monastery is the largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Yunnan Province, known as the "Little Potala Palace." It was built between 1679 and 1681 under the instruction of the Fifth Dalai Lama.

The monastery complex occupies a hillside and is designed to resemble the Potala Palace in Lhasa. The main buildings include Zhacang Hall (the main assembly hall) and Jikang Hall, along with numerous monk residences.

The monastery houses valuable religious artifacts and artwork, including ancient scriptures, thangka paintings, and gilded statues. It remains an active religious site with approximately 700 resident monks.

Visitor tips: The monastery is at 3,380 meters altitude. Take it slow and stay hydrated. Photography is not allowed inside the halls. Dress modestly and remove hats when entering temples.

sources.title: 噶丹·松赞林寺 - 百度百科
sources.content:
噶丹·松赞林寺 完整信息汇总

基本信息
别名：归化寺
所属地区：云南省迪庆藏族自治州
宗教类别：佛教（藏传佛教）
建成时间：1681年
海拔高度：3300多米
门票价格：115.00元
开放时间：07:30～18:30
建议游玩时长：3-5小时
最佳季节：3月-5月和9月-11月

寺院地位
该寺为"云南省规模最大的藏传佛教寺院"，也是康区知名大寺之一，系川滇地区黄教中心，在整个藏区具有重要地位，被誉为"小布达拉宫"。

建筑特色
"该寺依山而建，外形犹如一座古堡，集藏族造型艺术之大成，又有'藏族艺术博物馆'之称。"主殿为五层藏式建筑，下层大殿有108根柱子，可容纳1600人。

历史沿革
公元1679年兴建，公元1681年竣工。五世达赖喇嘛亲赐寺名。1936年贺龙率红二方面军长征途经，寺院支持红军。

宗教意义
"噶丹"表示传承黄教祖师宗喀巴创立之噶丹寺；"松赞"指天界三神；"林"即"寺"。

主要建筑
扎仓：主殿，僧众学习经典场所
吉康：副殿
八大康参：独克、扎雅、东旺、绒巴、洋朵、结底、卓、乡城

典藏文物
寺内收藏丰富，包括五世、七世达赖时期的"八尊包金释迦牟尼佛像、贝叶经、五彩金汁精绘唐卡、黄金灯"等，收藏《丹珠尔》十部，其中两部为金汁手书。

寺院管理体系
最高组织：拉西会议（由活佛、堪布、格西等高僧组成）
截止2012年：僧侣700余人

传说故事
"林木深幽现清泉，天降金鹬嬉其间"——寺院有终年不涸的清泉，常见一对金鹬出双入对。

参观提示
由于地处高海拔，即使8月也可能降雪。建议携带外套、羽绒服、防晒霜、太阳镜。6月至9月为雨季，春秋季最宜访问。

sources.title: Shangri-La Travel: The Majesty of Ganden Sumtseling Monastery
sources.content:
Shangri-La Travel: The Majesty of Ganden Sumtseling Monastery

Ganden Sumtseling Monastery (Songzanlin) in Shangri-La is an awe-inspiring Tibetan Buddhist monastery that truly earns its nickname as the "Little Potala Palace." The monastery sits on a hillside overlooking the town and surrounding landscape.

The complex is impressive in scale, with golden-roofed halls, numerous monk residences, and the serene Lamuyangcuo Lake (also known as Virgin Soul Lake) at its base. Walking around the lake takes about 50 minutes and offers beautiful reflections of the monastery.

The monastery remains very much a living religious institution, with monks going about their daily routines of prayer, study, and meditation. Visitors are welcome to observe respectfully.

The scenic area surrounding the monastery includes the lake, nearby villages, and hill viewpoints that provide panoramic vistas of the monastery against the mountain backdrop.
